matched_queries: Workers' rights to understand how tips and service charges are shared, request tipping records or challenge unfair allocation. Employer and tronc arrangements for distributing tips and communicating the policy to staff.

Discover UK guidance connected to employers' tipping policies, consultation with workers, policy reviews and worker feedback. Keep a connection to staff tips separate from tax treatment and from an assessment that wording must change.

passages.quote:
If you get tips at work they do not count towards the National Minimum Wage. You still have to pay Income Tax on tips and may have to pay National Insurance.

How tips are paid

You could get tips:

directly from a customer in cash or electronically, for example through a mobile app

as part of your pay packet from your employer

through a separate system for managing and sharing out tips at your workplace (known as a ‘tronc’)

How your employer handles tips

There is a statutory code of practice on the distribution of tips.

By law, all tips must be given to workers without deductions.

The code of practice has information on:`

the types of workers and tips covered by the legislation

how employers can ensure tips are distributed fairly and transparently

the need for a written tipping policy and accurate record-keeping

steps for resolving disputes, including escalation to an employment tribunal

Where to get help

Contact Acas if you have a question about tips or the National Minimum Wage.
